scope: Node web runtime with a real MySQL database

cases.name: fresh schema creates six InnoDB tables, JSON fields and lookup indexes
MySQL startup initializes one snapshot and all five matching projections
Admin, PM, Member login and anonymous access behave through the MySQL runtime
all 27 available module entries are served with the shared API bridge
Vietnamese, emoji, groups, guests and UTC offsets persist correctly in JSON and SQL
editing an unrelated field preserves participants, guest count and equipment quantities
room conflicts, invalid dates, capacity and failed participant batches leave SQL unchanged
maintenance, equipment booking limits and restoration update actual MySQL records
Member visibility, own RSVP and PM ownership are enforced with persisted state
room grants and role matrix persist and reject unauthorized PM writes
room, equipment and user CRUD sync projections and preserve soft-deleted rows
recurring conflicts roll back the whole series and valid series persist all occurrences
a real SQL trigger failure rolls back an earlier meeting INSERT and the snapshot
restart retains credentials, Unicode, groups, guests and equipment; old sessions expire
two web processes serialize concurrent account writes without losing records
SELECT FOR UPDATE blocks two processes; only one overlapping booking commits
read-only requests and suggestions do not rewrite the snapshot revision
killing an application connection during a real lock wait returns 503 and reconnects
cancellation retains history and releases all device bookings and reminders in SQL
old schemas fail without partial writes; migration is repeatable and preserves data
missing schema fails closed; a restored snapshot rebuilds matching projections

limitations: Node web store only; Java uses a separate schema and authentication contract
No production load, full penetration test, external integrations or real-device acceptance

nodeTestRunner.note: 21 scenario subtests plus one parent test
